Strait of Hormuz Status: October 9, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  223 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
9 October 2026 .
Brent $ 104.64 + 0.68 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 The IRGC says it attacked a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, per UA.NEWS, CNBC, and The Maritime Executive, with Financial Times reporting Iran has extended attacks beyond the strait into the Gulf.

02 Brent crude stood at $104.64, up 0.68% over 24 hours, as of 18:18 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

03 The IRGC has renewed warnings to vessels attempting to pass through a restricted zone south of the Strait of Hormuz, per IRNA.

Situation
Financial Times reports Iran has extended tanker attacks beyond the strait into the Gulf, a geographic escalation beyond what had previously been reported in this window. The IRGC, per IRNA, renewed its warning that vessels defying designated shipping routes and attempting to transit a restricted zone south of the strait will face consequences. A Vietnamese ship was among those struck in the strait, per The New Region. The LPG tanker targeted south of the strait, which Iranian state media reported the IRGC struck after claiming the vessel was on an unauthorized route, remains an unverified claim; the US has not confirmed the strike. Brent stood at $104.64, up 0.68% over 24 hours, as of 18:18 UTC. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, a fraction of the pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. This feed indexed 34 headlines in the last 24 hours. As of 18:20 UTC, 159 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
